Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. ns1:item.ns1:title: Berry curvature multipoles in Kagome superconductor CsV<sub>3</sub>Sb<sub>5</sub>
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77618-6

Higher-order nonlinear Hall responses can reveal Berry-curvature multipoles associated with electronic nematicity. Here, the authors identify a vortex-enhanced third-order Hall response in CsV3Sb5 and uncover a Berry-curvature quadrupole associated with chiral loop-current order

ns1:item.ns1:title: Autonomous robotic operation controlled by wave-based neuromorphic hardware
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77661-3

The authors demonstrate autonomous robotic control using wave-based neuromorphic hardware. Physical wave interference performs reservoir computing for obstacle recognition and real-time robot navigation, with a route toward solid-state implementations based on spin waves.
ns1:item.dc:title: Autonomous robotic operation controlled by wave-based neuromorphic hardware

ns1:item.ns1:title: Spontaneous formation of picoliter water bridges
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77515-y

Water evaporation at the microscale is primarily governed by vapor diffusion and capillarity, but the stability of picoliter water bridges remained poorly explained. Here, the authors demonstrate that adsorption at solid interfaces can significantly inhibit evaporation, thereby enabling the spontaneous formation and long-term stability of picoliter water bridges through an energy-minimization mechanism, as visualized by X-ray imaging.
ns1:item.dc:title: Spontaneous formation of picoliter water bridges
ns1:item.dc:creator: Gun Oh
Dohyeon Jeon
Sung Hoon Kang
Byung Mook Weon

ns1:item.ns1:title: Visible light suppresses carbon formation on Ni/CeO<sub>2</sub> catalyst in methane dry reforming reaction
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77706-7

Carbon deposition hampers the conversion of methane and carbon dioxide into syngas. Here, the authors use visible light to help oxygen move through a nickel-based catalyst, preventing carbon deposits while boosting methane conversion and hydrogen production.
ns1:item.dc:title: Visible light suppresses carbon formation on Ni/CeO<sub>2</sub> catalyst in methane dry reforming reaction

ns1:item.ns1:title: Strong coupling between RF photons and plasmons of electrons on liquid helium
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77527-8

Strong plasmon-photon coupling enables applications in plasmonics quantum technologies, yet dissipation is still a strong limitation. Here, the authors demonstrate a hybrid electron-on-Helium system where plasmons are strongly coupled to photons within an LC resonating circuit. This provides practical advantages and insight into Wigner crystal transitions and plasmon decay.
